**Job title:** Associate Director, Disease and Target Biology

**Department:** Disease and Target Biology; Data Science

**Location:** Oxford, United Kingdom

**Your impact begins here**

Lead a front-line scientific team that exploits human genetics, multi-omics, and patient data to deepen disease understanding and identify new opportunities for target discovery. As Associate Director, Disease and Target Biology, you will leverage your scientific and people leadership expertise to drive target discovery campaigns with our Therapy Areas and translate complex evidence into clear decisions. You and your team will work with the TAs to define the biological evidence needed to move targets and programmes forward across Type 2 Diabetes, Obesity, Cardiovascular, and Renal disease.

**What you'll bring**

You are an experienced scientific leader who can move confidently between detailed analysis, team development, and strategic decision-making. You bring strong expertise in human genetics and computational biology, along with the ability to explain complex evidence clearly to scientific and senior stakeholders.

Essential qualifications and experience:

* A PhD in human genetics, computational biology, genetic epidemiology, or a related discipline, together with substantial post-PhD experience.
* Experience combining genetics and omics with cohort or patient data to identify and stratify patient subgroups; and demonstrated experience applying this to actionable disease understanding and target discovery / validation.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience in drug/target discovery, with pharmaceutical, biomedical, or techbio industry experience strongly preferred.
* Experience leading and developing scientific teams, ideally across multiple locations, and comfortable remaining hands-on technically.
* Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to influence therapeutic area partners and senior leaders.

Useful, but not essential:

* Experience managing teams across sites or time zones.
* Direct experience in metabolic, cardiovascular, or renal disease.
* Familiarity with artificial intelligence and machine-learning approaches applied to biological and clinical data.
* An understanding of the drug discovery and development value chain.
* A strong publication record and standing in the external scientific community would also be valuable.

**What you'll do**

* Lead and develop a team of approximately seven scientists based across the UK and Denmark, taking responsibility for recruitment, performance, development, well-being and an effective cross-site working environment.
* Use human genetics, multi-omics and cohort or patient data to identify and stratify patient subgroups; applying results in pursuit of better disease understanding and testable hypotheses for target discovery.
* Co-lead scientific campaigns with therapeutic area teams, defining the biological evidence required to support or challenge hypotheses and enable programme decisions.
* Set the team's scientific and operational direction in partnership with Data Science leaders and colleagues across AI & Digital Innovation and Global Research.
* Guide the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in disease biology, work with engineering teams on deployment, and provide scientific leadership for academic and biotechnology collaborations.

**Who you'll work with**

You will join the Disease and Target Biology team within ADI Data Science and report to Robert Kitchen. The role leads approximately seven direct reports with varying levels of seniority and specialist expertise across the UK and Denmark.

Your closest partners will include Therapy Area colleagues working in Type 2 Diabetes, Obesity, Cardiovascular and Renal disease, as well as teams across Data Science, Data Engineering, AI & Digital Innovation and Global Research. You will also represent the organisation in relevant academic, biotechnology and industry collaborations. The wider geographical scope includes stakeholders in the UK, Denmark, the US and China.

**What you can expect here**

This is a player-coach opportunity for a scientific leader who wants to remain close to the work while building the capability and impact of a multidisciplinary team. You will have scope to shape scientific strategy; contribute directly to priority analyses and influence how biological evidence informs research decisions.

The role also provides opportunities to lead external collaborations, contribute to publications and conferences, and help advance the responsible use of patient and cohort data.

Oliver Wyman, a Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) business, is a management consulting firm driven by deep industry insight, bold innovation, and a collaborative approach that cuts through complexity to help organizations navigate their most defining transformative moments.

Clients approach us with their most significant challenges, and we assemble teams of experts to address each facet of these complex issues. Together, we create breakthroughs that lead to remarkable impact.

## Role Overview

Oliver Wyman DNA team builds software products and solutions that aim to be re-used and adapted across different contexts or projects. Typical products span solutions that improve how financial institutions model and manage risk, how wealth managers run their advisory and client processes, how lenders perform credit analysis, and how retailers personalize digital marketing, among others. AI is a key component of all our solutions, and most of our products are either AI-native or largely AI-enhanced.

  

As Director of Product Management, you help grow one or more of these products. You work closely with the product’s ecosystem of partners and are accountable for the product itself: what it does, who buys it, why they keep using it, what it costs to run, what it earns, and where it goes next. You will work with products from initial idea (early-stage propositions still proving their first commercial case) to scale (established products carrying live client deployments and renewal commitments). Stakeholders are based in UK, Europe, India and US time zones.

  

## Why Join Us?

* Own real, impactful products, used inside the firm and by our clients, and be accountable for where they go next
* Build products that materially improve how major institutions manage risk, advise clients, extend credit or reach their customers

**Commercial Product Ownership:**

* Proven ownership of a software product used at scale, internally or sold to external clients, with accountability for its performance.
* Track record of defining and defending a revenue model, pricing and packaging, and of managing the trade-off between investment, margin and product ambition.
* Fluency with the numbers behind a product: able to rebuild a product-level P&L, defend the method behind it, and use it to demonstrate business impact.

* Awareness of AI product economics, including inference and token cost per user, and how these shape pricing and unit economics.

  

* **Product Definition, Delivery and Quality:**

* Experience working with engineers and architects on product definition, testing, release readiness, security and support needs.
* Knowledge of the support, SLA and maintenance model that a commercially sold product requires.
* Fluency with product and delivery tooling such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence or equivalent.

  

**Go-to-Market, Sales Support and Communication:**

* Excellent written and verbal communication, and credibility in front of clients and partners.

  

**Stakeholder Alignment and Trade-Off Management:**

* Experience working across a product portfolio on alignment, reuse of shared components and investment trade-offs.

**A World-Changing Company**

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

### The Role

We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.

You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date.

Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three.

Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems.

### Technologies We Use

* Java, Scala, Rust, and Python
* Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution
* Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability
* Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage
* Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration

You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.

### What We Value

* Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimisers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing
* A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does
* Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack
* A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition
* Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback
* Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software

### What We Require

* Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience
* Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Rust, Scala, C++, or C
* Strong foundations in algorithms, data structures, and concurrency
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems
* Contributions to open-source projects

**🛠️****Procurement Team @ Bloom & Wild Group**

You’ll be joining the engine room of Bloom & Wild’s fastest-growing categories. While we are known for our flowers, our Procurement & Technical team owns end-to-end management of our non-horticultural range: from fresh-baked treats, chocolate and drinks to candles, home and lifestyle gifts.

As our gifting range grows, and more of it is our own brand, we’re expanding the team to bring technical expertise in-house alongside our Strategic Procurement and Supply Chain pillars. As our first dedicated technical hire for gifting, you’ll report to the Head of Procurement & Inventory and be the technical lead for every non-floral product we sell. The role is primarily UK-focused, with a smaller remit supporting our other European markets.

You’ll work closely with our Range, Strategic Procurement, Supply Chain, Brand and Warehouse teams, as well as our on-site quality team. This is a rare opportunity to build a technical function from the ground up and see your work directly protect our customers and our brand as we scale.

### ⚙️ What you'll be doing:

* **Own Non-flower Quality & Compliance End-to-End:** Be the technical lead for all our non-horticultural and add-on products, e.g. Food & Drink, Candles & Home Accessories, Pamper Products, Textiles. Define our requirements and standards based on product risk and proactively flag risks before they reach customers.
* **Build the Framework:** You’ll set up how we do quality and compliance for multi-category: risk assessment, product specifications (including clear sensory and acceptance criteria), testing and transit-testing requirements, and the structure of our quality and compliance platform.
* **Supplier Onboarding & Auditing:** Get involved early in the NPD process, working with Range and Procurement to assess the risk of new products and suppliers. Lead technical onboarding, from document reviews to on-site audits (to BRCGS standard) for higher-risk own-brand suppliers, such as ready-to-eat and allergen-sensitive products.
* **Technical Due Diligence:** Own the collection, review and auditing of technical, safety and regulatory documentation across all categories (food, drink, candles, toys and other gifting items), making sure our supplier & product information collation and due diligence is watertight.
* **Labelling & Regulatory Sign-off:** Own pre-launch sign-off of own-brand labels and customer-facing product information, including ingredients, allergens, CE/UKCA marks and category-specific warnings. Put controls in place so this stays accurate across every channel when a recipe or ingredient changes.
* **Issue & Incident Management:** Lead our response to quality incidents. Drive root-cause investigations with suppliers and/or fulfilment site leads, recommend balanced, practical solutions to senior stakeholders, and hold suppliers and warehouses to account on corrective actions. Lead engagement with regulators where needed.
* **Traceability & Recall Readiness:** Own our traceability and recall/withdrawal processes as a standing capability, including running regular mock recalls to test and improve them.
* **Surveillance Testing & Performance:** Introduce surveillance testing across our own-brand range so we catch issues before our customers do. Set and own quality KPIs for our supplier base and lead the quality elements of supplier reviews. Including monitoring and taking action related to customer complaints & quality metrics.
* **Own Site Quality Processes & Frameworks:** Take overall responsibility for the quality and compliance processes and frameworks at our sites for non-horticultural products. You’ll set the standards our warehouse teams work to, from intake checks and non-conformance handling to documentation and record-keeping, keep them up to date as our range evolves, and review site records to make sure they’re consistently applied. You’ll partner closely with our on-site fulfilment leaders and quality team, who carry out the day-to-day checks.
* **Regulatory Monitoring:** Keep on top of changes in food and product safety law and turn them into practical updates to our standards, both internally and with suppliers.

### ✅ You’ll love this role if you...

* **Have a strong food safety and technical background (5+ Years of Experience)** - You’ve worked in a food technical or quality role (retailer, brand or manufacturer side) and have solid grounding in HACCP, allergen management, specifications, risk assessment and UK food law. Food safety qualifications (e.g. HACCP or Food Safety Level 4, BRCGS auditor training) are a plus.
* **Are a confident supplier auditor and manager** - You’ve carried out on-site supplier audits and know how to hold suppliers to a clear standard, firmly and constructively. You’re willing and able to have regular supplier visits
* **Are a builder and a credible generalist** - You’ve built quality processes and frameworks, not just run them, and you’re comfortable applying quality and risk fundamentals beyond food (e.g. candles, toys, non-food gifts), bringing in specialist input where needed. You know how to prioritise your work effectively.

# Marketing Operations Manager

## Location

United Kingdom; Germany; Portugal; Spain

## Employment Type

OverviewApplication

## **About Pleo**

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

## **About the role**

We're looking for a Marketing Operations Manager to join our Marketing Operations, RevOps team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help build the operational infrastructure needed to support our upmarket expansion into Mid-Market and Enterprise segments and be part of our Marketing Ops team as we scale our spend management platform across growth companies in Europe. If you're excited about designing account-based go-to-market systems, establishing AI enablement across operational workflows, and solving complex cross-functional challenges, and are passionate about marketing operations, RevOps, and systems architecture, then this is the opportunity for you!

## **Who you’ll be working with and reporting to**

You’ll report to our Associate Director, Marketing Operations and work closely with teams in Marketing Operations, RevOps, and Sales Ops. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to powering how the marketing team runs—from campaign operations and reporting cadence through to AI adoption and process improvement. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across Data, BAT (Business Automation & Tools), CX Ops, and Engineering to ensure success and maintain a single account truth across systems.

## **What you’ll be doing**

As a Marketing Operations Manager, you will:

* **Build and refine marketing operational frameworks** – Lead initiatives to continuously improve campaign workflows, request intake, approval processes, team governance, MQL→MQA routing logic, and SDR/BDR handoff processes.
* **Own account intelligence and reporting cadence** – Design account scoring models for Mid-Market and Enterprise, maintain executive dashboards, integrate intent/firmographic/behavioral signals into segmentation, and manage account assignment logic.
* **Drive AI adoption across Marketing Ops** – Translate AI capabilities into operational reality by building processes, governance, and enablement that accelerate execution and scale output within the team.
* **Ensure tooling health and systems ownership** – Manage HubSpot workflows, automations, and integrations while coordinating with BAT and Engineering on tech stack builds, QA standards, and enterprise tooling requirements.
* **Enable team capabilities and documentation habits** – Upskill Marketing and Marketing Ops teammates through shared standards, QA checklists, repeatable guides, templates, and onboarding resources to raise the operational floor.

## **What you bring**

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

* **HubSpot Fluency** – A solid understanding of designing workflows, routing logic, and automation in HubSpot, including its limitations and when to extend outside the platform.
* **Account Operations Mindset** – Track record of building ABM operational processes, MQL-to-MQA scoring rules, multi-stakeholder buying committee motions, and AI/automation adoption that sticks.
* **Sales Ops Partnership** – Ability to collaborate seamlessly with Sales Ops on account strategy, territory strategy, handoff logic, and rep productivity without jargon.
* **Data & Documentation Habits** – Excellent habits in building auditable specs, validating data quality, and diagnosing root causes in data flows alongside Data and BAT teams.
* Experience with multi-touch attribution modeling, lifecycle marketing operations (nurture flows, recycling, engagement scoring), and ABM platforms / account intelligence tools.
* A background in seeing a company move upmarket to Mid-Market/Enterprise and building scalable, long-term GTM operations.

## **Why is this role a good fit for you**

This role is a good fit for you if:

* You are an operational thinker who naturally designs sustainable systems, governance, and frameworks rather than executing quick-fix tasks.
* You love working cross-functionally across Marketing, Sales Ops, and Data teams to streamline GTM processes and remove friction.
* You are energized by driving practical AI adoption and upskilling team members through documentation, templates, and shared standards.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

* You prefer operating in established, rigid systems rather than designing new account-based infrastructure in ambiguous environments.
* You look at marketing operations as purely executing inbound lead lists without considering account context or buying committees.
* You rely on tribal knowledge rather than maintaining clear, auditable documentation and QA standards for your builds.

## **How you’ll develop in this role**

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

* Lead the launch of our account segmentation model to directly power SDR assignments and Mid-Market/Enterprise routing.
* Collaborate with Data and Marketing Ops teams to clean up attribution, reporting, and lifecycle data so performance metrics are fully trusted.
* Grow your skills in AI enablement, enterprise GTM systems, and cross-functional RevOps alignment, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale.

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in advanced RevOps and enterprise go-to-market strategies.

## **The location**

Please note: We can hire on a hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

## **Show me the benefits!**

* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis
* 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

## **The interview process**

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

1. **Intro call:** A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. **Hiring Manager Interview:** A 45 mins chat with the hiring manager, to deep dive in your experience and role
3. **Pleo Challenge and Team Interview:** We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role
4. **Final Interview:** A final interview with a senior leader

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for this role, we received a vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

* CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!
* Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

## **About your application**

* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

# Senior Product Manager

UK-Remote

***This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK.***

**Role Summary**

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively. 

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades. 

That means there are interesting product *problems* to solve - not just features to deliver. 

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions. 

You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it. 

**How we work** 

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty. 

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions. 

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them. 

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something. 

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are. 

**Responsibilities**

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll: 

* **Understand the problem.** Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them.
* **Shape product direction.** Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities.
* **Practise continuous discovery.** Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data.
* **Turn uncertainty into learning.** Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction.
* **Make good product decisions.** Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue.
* **Measure whether things are getting better.** Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect.
* **Work iteratively.** Help the team deliver in small steps, learn from what happens and adapt rather than treating plans as fixed commitments.
* **Communicate your thinking.** Clearly explain problems, evidence, choices, trade-offs and learning to people with very different levels of technical and product knowledge.
* **Create strong feedback loops.** Use conversations, demos, reviews and other forums to get useful feedback early rather than presenting finished thinking late.
* **Work as part of a team.** Create the conditions in which designers, engineers and other specialists can contribute to product decisions rather than treating product management as something the PM does alone.
* **Look beyond the product interface.** Understand the wider service, including processes, systems and teams around it, and recognise when solving a user problem requires changing more than software.

**Experience and qualifications** 

**Essential** 

* Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience.
* Using creative problem solving to build software solutions.
* Demonstrate experience working as a Product Manager in a multidisciplinary digital product team, working closely with disciplines such as design, engineering, research and delivery.
* Experience using product discovery alongside delivery - for example, user research, data, experimentation and hypothesis testing - to understand problems and inform what a team should do next.
* Experience working with significant uncertainty or ambiguity: identifying what is known, what is assumed and what needs to be learned before making larger commitments.
* Experience taking complex problems and helping a team turn them into clear priorities, outcomes and practical next steps.
* Experience making product decisions using a combination of user evidence, data, organisational goals, technical constraints and product judgement.
* Experience communicating product thinking clearly to a wide range of people, including explaining evidence, uncertainty, trade-offs and why particular decisions have been made.
* Experience working collaboratively with people outside the immediate product team, particularly where different groups have different needs, incentives or perspectives.

**Particularly useful** 

We'd be especially interested in candidates who have experience of one or more of the following: 

* Working in an organisation going through significant product, digital or organisational transformation.
* Working in complex service environments where improving the user experience involves changes to technology, operations, policy or organisational processes - not simply changing an interface.
* Helping teams move towards more iterative, outcome-focused or evidence-led ways of working.
* Working in a mission-led, research, publishing, education, scientific or other knowledge-based organisation.

Experience of scholarly publishing is useful but isn't required. 

 

**What we're looking for in a Senior Product Manager** 

For us, seniority isn't about having a larger backlog or knowing more product framework: it's about judgement. 

You'll be able to take a complex and uncertain problem, help people understand it, decide what we most need to learn, bring a team together around a sensible course of action and change that course when the evidence tells us to. 

You'll be comfortable making decisions without perfect information while being clear about the assumptions and risks involved. 

And you'll help the people around you think more clearly about the product - not simply tell them what to build. 

**Working at PLOS** 

You'll join PLOS's Product team and work collaboratively with colleagues across Digital and the wider organisation. 

The role has no direct line-management responsibility. 

The job is fully remote. Some flexibility to work across time zones and occasional national or international travel may be required. 

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is **(UK)****£65,000 - £73,500****.**PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below. 

**BENEFITS:** 

* Private medical insurance
* Life assurance
* Income protection
* Personal accident insurance
* Pension with up to 10% employer match
* 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave
* Birthday and three winter holidays days off
* 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
* Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

**About PLOS**

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

**We’re committed to equal opportunity**

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out.

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all.

Visit plos.org/careers to learn more.

To learn more about how PLOS protects your privacy, see our Employee Privacy Notice.

## About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

## **Overview**

* CircuitHub is primarily built using a combination of Haskell, Nix, and PostgreSQL, deployed to both AWS and bare metal machines. We use a significant amount of open-source technology, and also try and give back where possible (for example, both Rel8 and Fast Downward Haskell bindings).
* CircuitHub spans a vast problem space. Challenges include computer vision (OpenCV), machine learning (PyTorch), hard optimization problems (Z3/MiniZinc/OR-Tools), and all the normal engineering challenges of building both web-based customer-facing and internal tooling.
* We work on manufacturing execution systems, enterprise resource planning, and robotics. An old video from Haskell Exchange 2019 hints at what we are up to on the robotics side. We have progressed significantly since then!
* These roles are remote (any location), in-person, or hybrid, depending on preference.
* We have offices in South Deerfield - USA, Cambridge, and London, UK.
* Salary depends on the candidate and location, but as guidance in the UK, a likely range is £80k to £125k and in the US $125k to $250k, with additional equity.
* CircuitHub has raised $45M from top-tier VCs and has been going for about ten years. CircuitHub is profitable, with tens of millions in revenue. Small team (CircuitHub is ~50 employees) with tremendous growth opportunity and low risk. We are aiming to 10x capacity through 2027 in both our existing Massachusetts factory and expand into Europe.

## Team/Environment/Role

Our R&D team is more than 20 people, with eight engineers working directly on the Haskell code base. We are looking to expand the team significantly this year. We have many exciting problems to solve, from robotic path planning to more conventional web products.

We are happy to consider candidates without commercial Haskell experience, but your other skills and experience would need to compensate. A possible profile, for instance, would be a professional robotics background with some hobbyist FP experience.

Conversely, for experienced Haskellers without experience in our domain, we will look for interests that correlate with what we are trying to accomplish. Life is too short to work on something you are not passionate about!

## Description

*This project is one of a number in competition for a studentship from the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Bath. If successful, this studentship is expected to commence 04 October 2027.*

*An alternative start date may be possible if agreed with your intended supervisors and the Doctoral College.*

***Project Description***

|  |
| --- |
| The transition towards low-carbon energy requires wind-energy technologies with increased efficiency, reliability and operational lifespan. Magnetic levitation offers potential for wind-energy systems by providing contactless rotor support, reducing friction, mechanical wear and maintenance requirements [1–4]. These characteristics make magnetic bearing technologies particularly relevant to the development of efficient and reliable wind-energy systems.  However, magnetic levitation introduces additional challenges associated with rotor dynamics. The low mechanical damping associated with contactless support can increase susceptibility to vibration, instability and external disturbances. In active magnetic bearing systems, controllers are employed to regulate the rotor position and maintain contact-free operation [1, 3, 4]. Variations in rotational speed and aerodynamic loading introduce further dynamic uncertainties, requiring control strategies capable of maintaining satisfactory performance over a range of operating conditions [3–6].  This project will investigate advanced control strategies for magnetically levitated wind turbines, with particular emphasis on robust control. Mathematical models describing the dynamic behaviour of the magnetic levitation system will be developed and used to design control strategies for rotor stabilisation, vibration attenuation and disturbance rejection under uncertain and variable operating conditions. Particular attention will be given to the nonlinear electromagnetic forces associated with magnetic bearings. Suitable nonlinear system representations will be considered to account explicitly for these effects within the control design. Robust control methods for nonlinear systems, including Lur’e system formulations and LMI-based stability and control conditions, provide a framework for addressing nonlinearities and model uncertainty [7, 8].  The project provides an opportunity to combine renewable-energy applications with dynamic modelling and advanced control design. The outcomes will contribute to ongoing research on magnetically levitated wind turbines and provide a basis for the future implementation and experimental validation of advanced control strategies on prototype systems. |

## Entry Requirements

An interest in dynamic systems, control, magnetic levitation systems and renewable-energy applications is desirable. Experience with mathematical modelling, system simulation, MATLAB/Simulink, Python or related computational tools would be advantageous. |

Applicants must have, or be about to obtain, a UK Honours degree 1st or 2.1, or international equivalent. A master’s level qualification would also be advantageous.

**Non-UK applicants, who are not currently studying in the UK, must meet the programme’s** English language requirement **before the application deadline – no exceptions will be considered.**

# Trading and Liquidity Strategy Lead

**About Quidax**

Quidax is where money meets limitless possibilities. We’re making it super easy for individuals, businesses, and fintechs in Africa to access crypto. Our goal? Providing real value for our customers today while shaping the future of money.

**About the Role**

We're looking for a hands-on Trading and Liquidity Strategy Lead who understands crypto markets from doing the work. You know how to read an Order Book, find liquidity, manage a position and explain what a trade actually earned after costs.

You'll help make sure customers can trade at competitive prices, with enough liquidity and reliable execution. That matters whether they're using Instant Swap, trading on our Order Book, working with the OTC Desk or building on our APIs.

A big part of your role will be looking at our markets and asking:

* **"Can someone actually trade at that price?"**
* **"Why is liquidity thinning out?"**
* **"What are we earning after costs, and what risk are we carrying?"**

You'll report directly to the **Chief Financial Officer (CFO)**. We want someone who spots problems early, makes sound trading decisions and follows through until things work better.

**What You’ll Be Owning**

**Keep Our Markets Healthy**

* Monitor spreads, Order Book depth, fill rates, time to fill and slippage across our core pairs, especially USDT/NGN.
* Investigate stale quotes, one-sided liquidity and unusual price moves. Work out whether the issue is market demand, available funds, a liquidity provider or a system problem.
* Compare our pricing with executable prices on relevant markets. Know when a local premium makes sense and when our own quotes need attention.

**Find Liquidity & Execute Well**

* Source and execute trades through approved exchanges and counterparties, choosing the right venue, order type and size for the trade.
* Support liquidity and execution for the OTC Desk and our trading products. Know when to split an order, use a limit order or source an OTC quote.
* Assess cross-exchange and arbitrage opportunities after trading fees, slippage, funding and transfer costs. Check that both sides can actually execute and settle.

**Make Pricing & Market Making Work Better**

* Review our quotes and spreads against market conditions, inventory and the full cost of execution. Recommend changes that balance competitive pricing with sustainable margins.
* Work with market makers and liquidity providers on reliable two-sided quotes, useful depth and consistent availability.
* Check whether liquidity partners are improving execution, not just adding volume. Address weak performance and recommend better sources where needed.

**Stay on Top of Positions & Risk**

* Track trading inventory, open orders, unsettled trades and counterparty exposure. Execute approved hedges and rebalancing trades within agreed limits.
* Work with Treasury Ops and Finance on funding, settlement, reconciliation, realised and unrealised P&L. Investigate differences rather than carrying them forward unexplained.
* Escalate limit breaches, pricing errors and suspected market abuse promptly. Keep clear trade records and follow approval controls, even when the market is moving quickly.

**Turn Market Insight into Better Operations**

* Give the CFO a clear view of market health, execution costs, P&L and emerging risks, with specific recommendations and follow-through.
* Work with Product and Engineering on price checks, liquidity alerts and trading tools that help us catch problems earlier.
* Document trading decisions, incident responses and handovers. Share what works so good execution does not depend on one person being available.

**Within your first 3 months, we'd like you to:**

* Understand our trading flows, liquidity sources, positions and controls well enough to operate confidently within your mandate.
* Establish a baseline for spreads, depth, fill rates, slippage and trading costs across priority pairs.

Growth Product Manager
About this role
We’ve just rebuilt Replika and we’re going through a renaissance, and our goal is exponential growth.
Your job is one number: the predicted revenue from every user who installs the app or hits the web funnel. How you move it is up to you — pricing, packaging, retention, activation, whatever the data points to — but realistically most of the win is in monetization, and that’s where you’ll live. Paywalls, offers, pricing tests, subscription mechanics. You take the same traffic and make it worth more.
This is a hands-on, experiment-driven role, not a strategy seat. You form the hypothesis, ship the test, read it honestly, and either scale it or kill it. You’ll work directly with product, engineering, and the CEO, and your changes hit millions of users within weeks, not quarters.
You’ll sit with our GTM teams — user acquisition, web, brand, and data — because revenue per install is a shared number. They bring the user in; you decide how much that user turns out to be worth. This isn’t a broad product role; we’ve got core product and activation covered. We’re hiring you because monetization is where you’ve spent your career, and it’s where you’re better than we are.
What You’ll Be Doing
Move predicted revenue per install and per web-funnel visitor. That’s the number you own. Everything else is a means to it.
Run monetization experiments end to end. Paywall placement and design, pricing, packaging, offers, trial mechanics, subscription flows — hypothesize, ship an A/B test, read it straight, and scale the winners.
Start from a playbook. You’ve run enough of these to know what usually works and what usually doesn’t, so you begin from patterns, not from zero.
Reach into activation or retention when the numbers say so. If a change there is the fastest path to more revenue, make the case and ship it, but monetization remains the center of gravity.
Keep a steady cadence of tests live. Size each opportunity before you spec it, prioritize by expected revenue impact, and always have the next tests ready, so the pipeline never goes quiet, even when engineering is the bottleneck.
Write short, clear specs: what triggers it, how it's A/B tested, and the rule for calling it. Engineering should be able to build it without a dozen follow-up questions.
Keep an honest record. Log every experiment, what you expected and what actually happened, and say so early when a call was wrong.
Partner with GTM. Revenue per install is shared with UA and web. You don't run ads or user acquisition, but you work closely with the people who do, and feed monetization signal back into how we acquire and price.
Work directly with product, engineering, and the CEO. You’ll be in the room when ideas form, not waiting for a brief.
What We’re Looking For
A product career spent mostly on monetization. Not a generalist who ran a pricing test once — someone whose main body of work is making consumer products earn more per user.
A real track record moving revenue. You’ve owned monetization metrics — ARPU, LTV, conversion, trial-to-paid — and you can show what you moved and how.
At least one original monetization idea you can point to. Something you came up with from first principles, not lifted from a competitor’s playbook. This is the bar that separates you from 99% of the field.
You run experiments as a matter of habit. You’ve designed and read A/B tests and made ship-or-kill calls off the results, not off opinion.
Strong analytical instincts. You pull and sanity-check your own data, size the audience before you write the spec, and you don't confuse a pretty chart with a real result.
You ship. Idea to spec to live to measured, fast.
You use AI tools in your work already — for research, specs, analysis, and moving faster day to day.
You take a position early and in writing, in your own words. Short, plain and to the point.
Fluent English. You can write a spec that doesn’t need rewriting.
Bonus Points
Experience monetizing a B2C subscription app, especially one where the value is hard to explain in a single line.
Deep familiarity with a mobile monetization and experimentation stack — paywall and pricing tooling, Amplitude, attribution/MMP setup, feature flags, server-side testing.
Experience with AI-native products or emotionally engaging consumer apps in the social, communication, relationship, or entertainment space.
You’ve worked web-to-app funnels, not just in-app monetization.
You’ve been an early or sole monetization owner and built the testing process where none existed.
What You’ll Get
Flexible job schedule and generous vacation policy.
Direct impact on millions of worldwide users within months.
Push the boundaries of applied AI in a consumer setting.
Fully remote, able to work CET hours.

About Replika
In 2017, no one knew what AI was supposed to be. We built the world's first consumer AI app. Two million people showed up in two months. Today it's over 40 million, and the thing they keep telling us hasn't changed: it helped. It made their life better, steadier, a little less alone.
Most AI is built for tasks, not for people. It gives you answers, but it doesn't care what you do with them. AI doesn't just need intelligence. It needs intention. Because the real question isn't just what AI can do. It's what AI is for.
When the world's leading researchers wanted to understand whether AI could actually change someone's life, they studied Replika, because there was nothing else to study. Motion Designer, Growth

RiverStone is seeking a proactive and delivery-focused Financial Crime Compliance Analyst to support the operation and continued development of RiverStone’s Financial Crime framework.

The successful candidate will have hands-on responsibility across financial crime activities including sanctions, AML, fraud, bribery and corruption, tax evasion, due diligence, screening, referrals, risk assessment, monitoring, reporting and training. The role will also support financial crime considerations arising from acquisitions, delegated arrangements and third-party relationships.  
   
This is a broad financial crime role suited to someone with experience in regulated financial services who is keen to develop deeper expertise within the insurance sector and take ownership of key processes.

Role in the Target Operating Model

* Operating the Financial Crime framework.
* Identifying and assessing financial crime risks.
* Maintaining effective financial crime policies, procedures and controls.
* Performing and overseeing financial crime screening and due diligence.
* Managing financial crime referrals and escalations.
* Supporting financial crime monitoring and assurance.
* Producing management information and governance reporting.
* Providing advice and support to the business.
* Responding to regulatory change and emerging financial crime risks.
* Collaborating with both Local and Group Compliance functions throughout RiverStone

* Monitor the effectiveness of fraud prevention controls.

* Ensure requirements remain aligned with regulatory developments and RiverStone’s business.

**About Kernel**

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

About the team
Restaurants run on a stack of tools that rarely talk to each other: one for delivery, another for online orders, another for reservations, another for loyalty, and a till that knows nothing about any of them. The same guest can look like three different customers across three different systems.
DashOS is DoorDash's platform for fixing that. It connects marketplace ordering, direct ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management, marketing and point of sale around one shared view of the guest, so every product gets smarter as the others are used. DoorDash launched DashOS publicly at Dash Forward in September 2026, and from 2027 more than 80,000 restaurants on leading POS and middleware partners.
DashOS Engineering brings together engineers from across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt into one global organisation, led from London. Our teams cover reservations and guest CRM, digital ordering and omnichannel loyalty, POS and self-order kiosks, AI-powered marketing and Voice AI, and the shared data and integration platforms that connect them. Each team owns its own roadmap. The shared mission is making them work as one system.
About the role
We're looking for a backend-focused Software Engineer to build the high-performance, highly available services that restaurants depend on every day, from booking a table on a Friday night to recognising a regular the moment they order. You'll work closely with other engineers, product managers and designers, and because DashOS is newly launched, you'll help shape how its products connect rather than inheriting decisions someone else already made.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will...
Design, build, test, deploy and improve backend services for customer-facing features used by restaurants and their guests in markets around the world.
Own features end to end, from technical design through to launch and ongoing support, including taking part in an on-call rotation to keep systems reliable.
Work on hard problems in data, latency and scale: unifying guest identity across channels, real-time availability search across thousands of venues, and integrations with the systems restaurants already run.
Build on DoorDash's global platform, so the features you ship can reach restaurants across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt markets rather than being rebuilt for each one.
Work in a modern engineering environment with frequent daily releases, feature flags and AI coding agents used across code review, deployment and debugging.
Partner with engineers, product managers and designers across London and other DashOS locations to decide what to build and how.
We're excited about you because...
You have 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, and a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
You've built and operated backend services or web applications in production, with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms and system design.
You're fluent in at least one modern backend language (we mostly use Python), and you're happy to pick up new languages and tools as the platform evolves.
You care about the people using what you build, and you take ownership of technical solutions from first design to production.
You use AI coding tools as part of how you work, or you're keen to, and you're comfortable reviewing and taking responsibility for what they produce.
You enjoy collaborating with cross-functional teams to solve problems that don't have an obvious answer yet.

Meet Sievo
We are Sievo – the leading procurement analytics SaaS company from Finland. We help the largest companies in the world, household brands like Levi’s, Kellogg’s and Mars, to generate cost savings, understand their procurement data, make data-driven decisions, reduce emissions, drive supply chain resilience, and beyond. The role
The Product Director of Data Products is responsible for making Community Data a success. What is Community Data? When 2% of global GDP runs through Sievo, patterns emerge that no single company could see on its own. Community Data is Sievo's aggregated, anonymized view across all of it – benchmarks, data management, supplier intelligence, and spend patterns from a dataset representing a significant slice of global corporate purchasing.
This role defines the future of our data's value and the solutions built on it, for our SaaS customers and beyond: from the customer problem to data governance and contribution incentives, to credibility, to pricing and packaging Community Data, to defending it as a durable moat. You will be reporting directly to the SVP Product.
This is one of the hardest problems at Sievo- and one of the most valuable.
What you'll be doing
Define what Community Data continues to become as a product – from the vision to the concrete product roadmap.
Design what and how customers contribute data and why they'd want to, balancing what they give up against what they get back.
Continue establishing the methodology and statistical credibility that make benchmarks and intelligence trustworthy enough to act on.
Own pricing and packaging: decide what's sold as a distinct data product versus bundled into the core SaaS platform.
Partner with sales and marketing to build the commercial motion and prove customers will pay.
Lead the team alongside an Engineering Manager, setting vision and strategy and guiding the team in the right direction, while they own delivery.
Represent Community Data at the leadership level as a strategic asset and moat, not a feature line.
To succeed in this role, you:
Have experience in (ideally B2B) SaaS and/or data products product management.
Have personally built and packaged a data or benchmarking product from an ambiguous starting point.
Have made real pricing and monetization decisions and can speak concretely to what worked and what didn't.
Proven ability to set vision and strategy autonomously, and to lead a team without a continuously pre-defined roadmap to fall back on.
Excellent communication skills in English; can translate a genuinely ambiguous, technical problem into a clear narrative for engineers, sales, and the CEO alike.
Strong analytical and statistical reasoning: comfortable with sample size, bias, and methodology questions, without needing to write the code or run the analysis yourself (that’s why you have a team).
AI is part of how you work, not just to move faster but to do things that weren't possible before.
Ambitious, outcome-driven, genuinely energized by an undefined problem rather than needing one handed to you.
What awaits you at Sievo
A senior, high-impact Product Director role owning one of Sievo’s most strategic product opportunities end-to-end, helping define Sievo’s overall product strategy and commercial growth with a direct line to the executive team.
Real ownership to define the future of Community Data as a product, from vision and roadmap to methodology, governance, pricing, packaging, and go-to-market impact.
Sievonians are ambitious, yet kind and supportive -you’ll work with an international team of 40+ nationalities, collaborating with smart, driven, and genuinely kind people.
Our Finnish roots run deep: we are founded on an open, honest and transparent Nordic working culture where we value freedom and responsibility, while working with high standards. We are looking for people who yearn for this freedom, are able to make the most out of it and are willing to take on the responsibility.

# The Sparta Code

**Understanding is non-negotiable**

***Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.***

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

**Ask for forgiveness, not for permission**

***Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.***

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

**Fall in love with the problem**

***The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.***

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

**It's your fault. Lucky you.**

***If it's on you, it's in your control.***

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

**Conflict is a gift**

***Honesty is an expression of care.***

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

* Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.

* PMS analytics

* Experience inventorying and testing a large API and data surface end to end.

We’re looking for someone with a strong interest in finance, excellent attention to detail and the confidence to work with numbers and data. You don’t need to tick every box, but we’d love to hear from you if you have most of the following:

* **Strong Microsoft Excel skills** – you’re confident working with spreadsheets, manipulating data, using formulas and investigating discrepancies. Excel is a key part of this role, and an Excel skills assessment will form part of the recruitment process.
* Experience working in a finance team, accounts department or similar administrative role.
* Strong numeracy and literacy skills, with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
* A logical, analytical approach and the ability to investigate problems, identify errors and work out how to resolve them.
* Good IT skills and the confidence to learn new systems, including computerised accounting packages.
* Experience of finance tasks such as payment processing, refunds and balance sheet reconciliations.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a professional and customer-focused approach.

* AI-native: analysts use AI daily and build reusable methods that the whole team adopts.

* Weekly 1:1s and team syncs, plus case and partner-delivery rhythms.

# Mental Health Recovery Worker

### Job Introduction

**Recovery Worker - Ashford Recovery House**

Everyone’s Turning Point is unique. It’s the moment someone realises they’ve taken a small but significant step forward. Often, that step becomes the beginning of something bigger - but only when the right support is there at the right time. At Ashford Recovery House, you will be part of those moments every day.

Our established 24‐hour crisis service provides up to five days of intensive support for individuals experiencing acute emotional distress or a mental health crisis. The environment is calm, therapeutic and designed to help people feel safe and grounded. Guests have access to quiet spaces, social areas and a sensory environment that supports emotional regulation. Throughout their stay, they are encouraged to take an active role in their own recovery through personalised assessment, structured one-to-one sessions and ongoing review.

This is an exciting and rewarding place to work. The pace is dynamic, the work is emotionally meaningful, and no two days are the same. You will be supporting people at some of the most vulnerable moments in their lives, helping them de-escalate distress, explore coping strategies and reconnect with their strengths. If you thrive in a role where compassion, calmness and emotional intelligence truly matter, you will feel at home here.

### Role Responsibility

As a Recovery Worker, you will provide person‐centred, recovery‐focused support to individuals in crisis. You will spend time getting to know each guest, understanding their immediate needs and helping them make sense of what they are experiencing. A key part of your role will be delivering structured one-to-one sessions using Turning Point’s established Recovery Packs and mental health focused tools. These sessions help guests explore their emotions, identify triggers, develop coping strategies and build confidence in managing their mental health.

You will offer emotional support throughout each shift, helping individuals de-escalate distress and regain a sense of safety. You will also support guests with medication self-administration where required, maintain accurate daily records and incident reports, and ensure the service remains safe, clean and therapeutic in line with infection-prevention standards.

As part of preparing guests for their return home, you will help them identify what support they may need in the community and signpost them to appropriate services. You will work collaboratively with their circle of support including family members, carers and external professionals to ensure continuity of care and a smooth transition out of crisis.

The service operates on a 24‐hour basis, and you will work a combination of day shifts (8am–8pm), night shifts (8pm–8am), weekend shifts and sleep‐ins depending on the needs of the service. The night posts are dedicated waking night roles, involving primarily lone working, supported by an on‐site sleep‐in colleague who can be called upon in an emergency. We are recruiting for both Day and Night Roles.

### The Ideal Candidate

You do not need previous experience in mental health to join us. We welcome applicants with **basic experience in health or social care**, and we will provide full training, supervision and development opportunities to help you grow confidently into the role. What matters most is your ability to support people with empathy, patience and emotional resilience.

You will bring a genuine desire to help individuals move forward in their recovery, along with the maturity to work within a positive, person‐centred and non‐judgmental framework. You will be someone who can remain calm and grounded when supporting people who are distressed, overwhelmed or struggling to cope. Strong communication skills are essential, as you will be working with people from all backgrounds and liaising with a range of professionals.

The role requires basic health care skills such as supporting with medication, recognising signs of emotional or physical deterioration, maintaining accurate records and following safeguarding and risk management procedures. You will also be confident using structured tools and resources during one to one sessions, helping guests explore their experiences in a safe and supportive way.

We value the personal interests and skills you can bring to the service  whether that’s art, music, cooking, sports or something entirely different. These interests often become meaningful tools for connection and engagement, helping guests feel more at ease and more able to express themselves.

In return, you will be part of a supportive team, working in a service where your contribution genuinely matters. You will gain valuable experience in crisis support, emotional intervention and recovery‐focused practice, with opportunities for ongoing training and career progression within Turning Point.

## Description

**Job Requirements**   

# **Position Summary:**

At ILM, Senior Effects Technical Directors operate at the intersection of aesthetic design and technical simulation, tasked with creating advanced procedural setups, simulations, and particle and fluid systems for feature films and episodic series. We seek an artist with strong problem-solving abilities and a keen creative eye, capable of translating vague briefs into distinct visual options through rapid prototyping to establish a creative direction for both stylized effects and natural phenomena.

The ideal candidate is capable of building comprehensive systems that empower the broader team to efficiently execute complex tasks across multiple shots. They thrive in a dynamic, collaborative environment and consistently strive to deliver work of the highest quality.

  

# **What you’ll do:**

* **Visual Development & Rapid Prototyping:** Translate conceptual, often vague briefs into multiple distinct visual directions. Develop quick but highly polished look-dev tests and slap comps to help Directors and VFX Supervisors easily understand and lock in the creative language for both complex stylized phenomena and highly realistic natural simulations.
* **Technical Setup Architecture:** Design and build comprehensive, highly procedural FX systems from scratch—including RBD, fluid, cloth, and particle simulations. Set up and wrangle these simulations for large-scale, effects-driven visual effects shots, ensuring master setups output consistent results across entire sequences.
* **User-Centric Engineering & Rendering:** Ensure master setups are logically organized, optimized, and ready for handover, removing technical friction so shot artists of varying skill levels can run them efficiently. Establish baseline rendering and lighting workflows, and create or modify surface and volumetric shaders to reduce render times and maintain visual consistency across the broader team.
* **Troubleshooting & Problem Solving:** Serve as a key technical resource for the show. Solve complex technical problems and debug intricate simulation and rendering issues once setups are deployed to the wider floor. Pick up new techniques quickly and with ease, continuously raising the benchmark for quality and efficiency.
* **Collaboration, Support, & Mentorship:** Partner iteratively with FX Supervisors and Leads to refine effects through both the visual exploration and technical build phases. Drive seamless handovers by providing clear walkthroughs and documentation, while actively mentoring, coaching, and offering creative and technical guidance to artists of all levels.

  

# **What we’re looking for:**

* Extensive experience as a Senior Effects Technical Director in feature films and/or episodic TV.
* Ability to work with proficiency, energy, and passion within a team environment.
* Engages in the creative process with an inclusive and encouraging approach.
* Demonstrates an excellent aesthetic eye and has the technical know-how to achieve a desired look.
* Demonstrates strong problem-solving abilities and proactively contributes ideas and suggestions.
* Advanced proficiency in most aspects within Houdini.
* Experience and interest in contributing to talent development in the effects department.
* Linux and scripting proficiency.
* Please provide a demo reel that showcases your experience and technical skills.

## Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason - the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.
We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.
Here’s what this particular role covers.
🛠️ About our Engineering Teams
Wayve’s Robot Software group turns new vehicle programs into stable, reliable robot systems. The Platform Integration team works at the boundary between onboard software and vehicle hardware, bringing up new platforms while building reusable components and frameworks that make every future integration faster and more predictable.
As a Software Engineer on the Platform Integration team, you’ll combine hands-on vehicle and bench work with production software development. Your work will directly enable safe, scalable deployment across multiple vehicle programs.
🧠 Your day-to-day
Support software bring-up on benches, HiL systems, and vehicles, including work at international test locations.
Develop and maintain vehicle-facing software components and shared frameworks.
Diagnose integration issues across software and hardware boundaries and drive them through resolution.
Identify architectural improvements that reduce bespoke work and improve reuse.
Build diagnostics, tooling, and metrics for robot-software reliability and performance.
Produce clear documentation and runbooks for long-term supportability.
Collaborate with hardware, safety, controls, calibration, and reliability teams.
🧩 What you’ll be working on
New vehicle-program bring-up across embedded compute, sensors, networks, and software services.
Linux-based robotic and automotive systems with multi-process and distributed architectures.
ROS2 or similar middleware, node development, message interfaces, and system integration.
Sensor calibration, synchronisation, data validation, and system-level debugging.
Automotive-grade compute platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE and Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride.
Vehicle communication systems including CAN and Automotive Ethernet.
Shared abstractions and frameworks that improve reliability across programs.

You have strong software-development experience in C++, Python, or Rust.
You have delivered production-quality software on Linux-based robotic, embedded, or automotive platforms.
You understand ROS2 or similar robotics middleware and distributed-system integration.
You have hands-on experience integrating software with vehicle or embedded hardware.
You can diagnose complex problems using logs, telemetry, on-target tests, and systematic experimentation.
You understand vehicle sensors, networking, and the practical realities of platform bring-up.
Experience with drive-by-wire systems, CAN tools, shared frameworks, HiL or simulation, functional safety, technical documentation, or observability would be valuable.

We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.
Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere.
